scenario.ground_truth:
Affected component: router2 RIP version
Mechanism: router0 and router1 run RIPv2; router2 was switched
  to RIPv1. The two versions use different packet formats and
  v2 peers drop v1 updates by default (and vice versa). router2
  is "sending" updates that router1 ignores. router2's own
  connected networks stay in its RIB; only advertised ones
  vanish elsewhere.
Localization: router2
Root cause: RIP version mismatch (router2 v1, neighbors v2)
Fix: `vtysh -c "router rip" -c "version 2"` on router2

agent.diagnosis_text:
After a recent configuration change, router2 was set to RIP `version 1`
globally, while router1 is configured for RIP `version 2`. This creates
a strict bidirectional version mismatch on the wan_r1_r2 link
(20.20.0.0/8, router1 eth3 ↔ router2 eth2).

FRR's `show ip rip status` confirms the mechanism precisely:
router1 enforces `send version 2, receive version 2` on all interfaces,
including eth3. When router2 sends RIPv1 broadcast updates (to
255.255.255.255), router1 identifies them as version-mismatch packets
and discards them — directly evidenced by `BadPackets: 3` recorded
against gateway 20.20.0.2 on router1. Conversely, router2 enforces
`send version 1, receive version 1`, so it also discards router1's
RIPv2 multicast updates — recorded as `BadPackets: 4` against gateway
20.20.0.1 on router2.

The routes 1.0.0.0/8 and 128.168.0.0/16 are connected networks on
router2, advertised via the `network` statements in its RIP config.
They were last successfully propagated to router1 before the `version 1`
change took effect. At the time of investigation they were still present
in router1's RIP table with ~01:59 left on their 180-second expiry timer
(i.e., actively aging out and not being refreshed). All other routes in
router1 (learned from router0 via eth2) are unaffected because router0
uses RIPv2.

Root cause: router2's RIP daemon was reconfigured to `version 1`,
breaking compatibility with the `version 2`-only policy on router1.

Corrective fix: On router2, change the RIP global version back to 2
(`router rip` → `version 2`) so that both routers send and receive
RIPv2 multicasts on the wan_r1_r2 link. Routes will reconverge within
one update interval (≤30 seconds after the fix is applied).

per_axis.rationale: The report explicitly identifies router2 as the device misconfigured to RIP version 1 and localizes the issue to router2.
The submission explicitly identifies a RIP version/protocol mismatch—router2 running RIPv1 while router1 runs RIPv2—as the root cause.
The agent explicitly recommends setting router2's RIP to version 2 (router rip → version 2), which matches the expected corrective fix.

The agent's investigation log shows configuration and RIP-status observations (including version settings and BadPackets counters) that directly support the diagnosis; the writeup ties these observations to the logical mechanism (version-mismatch causing discarded updates and aging routes).
